bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Govt Goes Paperless; CM Choudhary, Ministers Get iPads - Oneindia News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Govt Goes Paperless; CM Choudhary, Ministers Get iPads India oi-Prakash KL By Oneindia Desk Published: Saturday, November 28, 2026, 9:58 [IST] Add as a preferred source on Google Bihar has joined the ranks of states moving their top-level governance online, rolling out a new e-cabinet system that puts the latest iPads into the hands of the chief minister, his deputies, cabinet ministers, and top bureaucrats, Hindustan Times reported. The digital transition comes with a price tag of over ₹2.20 crore. However, state officials believe the investment will pay for itself within six to seven months by cutting down on massive printing bills, paper usage, and the physical transport of heavy file bundles. By shifting to tablets, the administration hopes to fast-track urgent proposals that previously got bogged down in manual handling. AI Summary AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors Bihar launched an e-cabinet system using iPads for ministers and bureaucrats, costing over ₹2.20 crore, aimed at reducing paper usage and speeding up approvals. As the 12th state to digitize cabinet proceedings, its first digital session cleared 34 proposals, including the Patna water supply project under the AMRUT 2.0 scheme. Switch To Shorts With this launch, Bihar has become the 12th state in the country to digitize its cabinet proceedings. The inaugural digital session saw the clearance of 34 proposals, highlighted by a major administrative nod for the Patna water supply project under the AMRUT 2.0 scheme. Built by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), the new e-cabinet platform is locked to authorized iPads managed directly by the cabinet secretariat. Additional Chief Secretary (Cabinet) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary noted that while the primary interface lives on these tablets, a stripped-down version of the app is also accessible on select Android-based laptops. Getting the system up and running required roughly six weeks of trial runs and hands-on training for both politicians and bureaucrats. Still, adapting to the tech remains a hurdle. While a cabinet secretariat official pointed out that ministers are already issued high-end laptops by their departments, one senior minister admitted that in day-to-day practice, personal assistants do most of the actual operating-training sessions notwithstanding. Because of the learning curve, physical files aren't vanishing overnight. For the next few weeks, the administration will run a hybrid setup. "Both systems of the cabinet meeting, physical as well as e-cabinet, will run concurrently for the next few weeks before finally discontinuing the presentation of hard copies," HT quoted Chaudhary as saying. Speaking at a meeting on Friday, the Chief Minister framed the e-cabinet rollout as a cornerstone for greener, more transparent, and people-centric governance. Beyond just saving trees and time, he urged officials to simplify administrative workflows by integrating newer tools-specifically pointing to Artificial Intelligence-into the digital system moving forward, ANI reported. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans to revive sugarcane cultivation in Saharsa, targets 200 acres this year
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News The Bihar Sugarcane Development Board is preparing to revive sugarcane cultivation in Saharsa district, where the area under the crop has declined significantly over the years. The department has launched an initiative to bring 200 acres under autumn sugarcane planting this year, offering farmers free seed, subsidies and technical training, Gaon Junction reported. The plan also takes into account the proposed establishment of a new sugar mill in the district. To support its future operations, the department aims to expand sugarcane cultivation to 15,000–20,000 hectares across Saharsa and neighbouring areas. Under the scheme, farmers taking up sugarcane cultivation for the first time will receive free seed for up to one acre, subject to field verification. Existing sugarcane growers will be provided improved varieties of seed at a 50% subsidy. The department is also training farmers in scientific and modern cultivation practices to improve productivity. To help farmers produce quality planting material, the department arranged training at the Krishi Vigyan Kendra in Pusa on preparing sugarcane nurseries. Participants were also given the materials required to establish nurseries free of cost. Following the training, farmers have started preparing nurseries on their fields using the methods demonstrated. Sugarcane cultivation in Saharsa had reportedly declined to just 10–20 acres in recent years. The department now aims to increase the area to 200 acres through the autumn planting campaign. Shubham Kumar, Assistant Director of the Saharsa Sugarcane Development Board, said the department was working to revive sugarcane cultivation across the Kosi region and expand the area under the crop. Awareness campaigns are being conducted among farmers, with plans to bring more land under cultivation in the coming years. Around two decades ago, the Kosi region was among Bihar’s important sugarcane-growing areas. Villages such as Amarpur, Baluaha, Sitanabad, Nariyar, Rahuamani, Bishanpur, Bengaha, Balwa Haat, Sahuriya and Suhath in Saharsa district had substantial sugarcane cultivation. At the time, railway rakes carrying sugarcane were sent daily from Sonbarsa Kachari station to the Hasanpur sugar mill. Farmers received prompt payment after delivering their cane to the mill, making the crop an important source of regular income. However, the closure of Hasanpur sugar mill gradually reduced farmers’ interest in sugarcane cultivation, leading to a decline in the area under the crop. The proposed new mill and the department’s expansion programme are now aimed at bringing sugarcane production back to the region.

न्यूज | बक्सर . सरकारी संस्थानों और सार्वजनिक भवनों की सूरत बदलने के लिए जिला प्रशासन की ओर से सेवा संकल्प-सह-कायाकल्प अभियान चलाया जा रहा है। मुख्यमंत्री सम्राट चौधरी के निर्देश पर संचालित इस अभियान के तहत विद्यालयों, स्वास्थ्य केंद्रों, पंचायत भवनों, सामुदायिक भवनों और छात्रावासों की आधारभूत सुविधाओं को बेहतर बनाने की कवायद तेज की गई है। इसका उद्देश्य सरकारी परिसरों को स्वच्छ, सुंदर और सुव्यवस्थित बनाना है। आम लोगों को बेहतर सुविधाएं उपलब्ध कराना भी लक्ष्य है। अभियान के तहत विभिन्न सरकारी भवनों का निरीक्षण कर उनकी मौजूदा स्थिति का आकलन किया जा रहा है। जरूरत के अनुसार साफ-सफाई, रंग-रोगन, भवनों की मरम्मत, परिसर का सौंदर्यीकरण, पेयजल, शौचालय और बिजली की व्यवस्था दुरुस्त करने पर जोर दिया जा रहा है। विद्यालयों में विद्यार्थियों को बेहतर शैक्षणिक माहौल देने के लिए कक्षाओं को व्यवस्थित किया जा रहा है। परिसर की सफाई पर काम हो रहा है। शौचालयों की मरम्मत की जा रही है। पेयजल की सुविधा सुनिश्चित की जा रही है। स्वास्थ्य केंद्रों में मरीजों की सुविधा को ध्यान में रखते हुए स्वच्छता, प्रतीक्षालय, शौचालय और पेयजल की व्यवस्था बेहतर करने पर ध्यान दिया जा रहा है। जिला प्रशासन का लक्ष्य सरकारी भवनों को महज उपयोग की संरचना के बजाय स्वच्छता, बेहतर व्यवस्था, गुणवत्तापूर्ण जनसेवा के केंद्र के रूप में विकसित करना है। जिलाधिकारी नियमित कर रहे योजनाओं की समीक्षा पंचायत और सामुदायिक भवनों की मरम्मत, रंग-रोगन, सौंदर्यीकरण किया जा रहा है। इन्हें ग्रामीण स्तर पर प्रशासनिक गतिविधियों, सामुदायिक आयोजनों के लिए सुविधाजनक बनाया जा रहा है। छात्रावासों में भी स्वच्छता, पेयजल, प्रकाश, शौचालय समेत अन्य आवासीय सुविधाओं को दुरुस्त करने पर जोर है। जिला प्रशासन अभियान के तहत किए जा रहे कार्यों की नियमित समीक्षा कर रहा है। संबंधित विभागों और प्रखंड स्तरीय पदाधिकारियों को कार्यों में गुणवत्ता, समयबद्धता, जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश दिया गया है। काम में लापरवाही या अनावश्यक देरी bihar_raw_news.title: AIIMS Patna to Establish Bihar's First Skin Bank - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next AIIMS Patna to Establish Bihar’s First Skin Bank 28 Nov 2026 1 min read Why in News? The Bihar Government has approved ₹3.07 crore for establishing the state's first Skin Bank at the Burns Centre of AIIMS Patna during the financial year 2026–27. Key Points Purpose: The facility will support the treatment of patients suffering from severe burn injuries and complex wounds. Function of Skin Bank: It will store human cadaveric skin , which can be used as a biological dressing to provide temporary coverage for burn wounds. Benefits: Donated skin helps reduce fluid loss, protects exposed tissues and minimises the risk of infection. Infrastructure: The project will involve dedicated infrastructure and specialised equipment for skin retrieval, processing, preservation and storage. Significance: The facility is expected to strengthen specialised burn care services in Bihar and the wider eastern region. bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi– Bihar bus service opens on 18 routes with fixed fares - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Delhi–Bihar bus service opens on 18 routes with fixed fares Breaking News Delhi–Bihar bus service opens on 18 routes with fixed fares By Ayesha Siddiqui November 28, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp A new Delhi–Bihar bus service has been launched on 18 interstate routes, with more than 200 buses planned and fares fixed across different vehicle categories, according to Live Hindustan – NCR. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi Transport Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh and Bihar Transport Minister Damodar Rawat flagged off the service from the Kashmere Gate Inter-State Bus Terminal on Friday. The service was introduced under an agreement between the Delhi and Bihar governments. According to the report, Delhi’s Transport Department has issued 216 permits to the Bihar government for operating buses on the 18 routes. The services will connect Delhi with 13 cities and areas in Bihar, although the report does not provide a complete route-wise list. The fixed fares vary by distance and bus category. For Patna, the reported fares are ₹1,615 for a non-air-conditioned seater, ₹1,715 for a sleeper, ₹1,980 for an air-conditioned seater and ₹2,919 for an air-conditioned sleeper. For Darbhanga, the fares are ₹1,592, ₹1,692, ₹1,853 and ₹2,866 respectively. The reported fares for Bhagalpur are ₹1,917 for a non-AC seater, ₹2,017 for a sleeper, ₹2,347 for an AC seater and ₹3,256 for an AC sleeper. For Araria, the corresponding fares are ₹1,929, ₹2,029, ₹2,362 and ₹3,276. Delhi officials said the service would make travel easier for people from Bihar living and working in the capital. Singh said the initiative could benefit between 15 lakh and 20 lakh people in Delhi, while Rawat said it would provide direct bus connectivity to 13 destinations in Bihar. The fixed-fare structure is also intended to limit arbitrary fare increases by private bus operators, particularly during festivals and periods of high demand, the report said. The service adds an inter-state public transport option from Kashmere Gate, a major bus terminal in north Delhi. The report does not specify the operating frequency, detailed departure schedules or the names of all 18 routes. These details will be important for passengers assessing the service’s availability and coverage. national_raw_news.content: Women and Child Development Minister Annpurna Devi has said that the Government is working to ensure that every child of the country gets a safe childhood and an opportunity to study. She said that the Government is committed to fulfilling the goal of Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat by 2030. The Minister spoke at an event in New Delhi yesterday to mark the second anniversary of the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The campaign, launched on the same day in 2024, aims to eliminate child marriage through a ‘whole of Government’ and ‘whole of Society’ approach. Ms Devi said that women are leading the development journey of India, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of women-led development. She said that the campaign reminds society to stop child marriage. Highlighting that girls’ education is the most effective means of preventing child marriage, she called on all citizens to actively participate in achieving the goal of a child marriage-free India by 2030. Ms Devi said that recognising India’s efforts in eradicating child marriage, the United Nations has declared 27th November as the International Day to End Child, Early and Forced Marriage. Speaking on the occasion, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat is not just a government campaign, but a collective commitment to give every girl child in the country education, dignity and the opportunity to fulfil her dreams. Ms Gupta stressed that the percentage of women who got married before the age of 18 have declined from 23.3 per cent in 2019-21 to 20.1 per cent in 2023-24.

national_raw_news.title: CDS General N S Raja Subramani stresses India must develop indigenous defence capabilities to sus...
national_raw_news.content: Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani stressed that India must develop its own approach to future warfare, taking lessons from global conflicts while keeping its unique security challenges in mind. He said this while delivering a lecture on the future of warfare and India’s preparedness for multi-domain operations in New Delhi yesterday. In his lecture, General Subramani highlighted that Atma Nirbharta in defence is not merely a slogan but essential for the country to sustain future military operations. The CDS also stressed that modern warfare is shifting from network-centric to decision-centric operations, with greater reliance on artificial intelligence, persistent surveillance and integrated military capabilities. General Subramani also emphasised that India must strengthen coordination among its three services and develop a joint communication network to enable faster decision-making. He also called for greater focus on space-based assets, cyber defence, electronic warfare and subterranean warfare. Drawing lessons from conflicts involving Israel, Iran, Russia and Ukraine, the CDS highlighted the importance of intelligence, long-range precision strikes, drones, artificial intelligence and cyber capabilities. He also stressed that technological superiority alone cannot win wars, as trained manpower, logistics, industrial capacity and reliable allies remain equally important. Meanwhile, citing Operation Sindoor, General Subramani praised the coordination among the armed forces, precision targeting and the effectiveness of indigenous systems such as BrahMos and Akash.

national_raw_news.title: IFFI to draw its curtains today in Goa, bringing 9 days of cinematic brilliance, artistic express...
national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will draw its curtains today in Goa, bringing nine days of cinematic brilliance, artistic expression and cultural exchange to a close. The final day will feature screenings of four films – Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Health Centre, Azad Bharath and We Are All Strangers, directed by Anthony Chen, which has been selected as the festival’s closing film. The closing ceremony will be held this evening at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium in Panjim, where outstanding cinematic achievements will be honoured through the festival’s prestigious awards. Akashvani correspondent reports that the 2026 edition of India’s cinematic carnival in Goa has been a magnificent confluence of stories, cultures and creative expressions from across the world. The nine-day celebration, which began on the 20th of this month, showcased more than 150 international films from 86 countries, alongside 76 films in 18 languages in the Indian Panorama section. A major highlight of this year’s IFFI is the sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow, bringing together 100 aspiring filmmakers across 13 filmmaking crafts. Adding another feather to Prasar Bharati’s creative outreach, its first-ever script pitching initiative, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’, provided emerging writers a national platform to present original stories in ten Indian languages and connect with the film industry. The festival also hosted 14 sessions featuring masterclasses, workshops and panel discussions, bringing together acclaimed filmmakers and industry professionals. Strengthening its global industry connect, the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar attracted 2,288 delegates from 54 countries, including 471 buyers, opening up new avenues for international collaborations and co-productions. Notably, IFFI 2026 brought together 52 women filmmakers and 62 debut filmmakers, celebrating fresh perspectives and nurturing the next generation of cinematic talent. The closing ceremony will celebrate excellence in world cinema, with the coveted Golden Peacock for Best Film and Silver Peacock honours for Best Director and Best Actor in Male and Female categories among the major awards. The ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal will also recognise a film promoting peace, tolerance and intercultural understanding. As Goa prepares to bid farewell to another memorable edition, IFFI leaves behind more than just a collection of films – it leaves a celebration of imagination, creativity and the enduring power of stories to transcend borders and bring the world together.

national_raw_news.title: Treesa-Gayatri enter Syed Modi International semi-finals, eye third successive title 27 Nov 2026 | 7:59 PM 87
national_raw_news.content: Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have moved a step closer to winning their third consecutive women’s doubles title at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 Badminton Tournament. Meanwhile, Tanvi Sharma and Unnati Hooda have entered the women’s singles semi-finals. Top seeds Treesa and Gayatri advanced to the semi-finals after receiving a walkover from seventh-seeded French pair Margot Lambert and Camille Pognante in the quarter-finals. In women’s singles, second seed Tanvi Sharma defeated Indonesia’s Ni Kadek Dhinda Amartya Pratiwi in a hard-fought three-game encounter, 21-19, 18-21, 21-14. Third seed Unnati Hooda also secured a hard-fought victory over compatriot Anmol Kharb, winning 21-19, 15-21, 21-18. With Tanvi and Unnati set to face each other in the semi-finals, an all-Indian finalist in women’s singles is now assured. In the other semi-final, top seed Riko Gunji of Japan will take on fourth seed Supanida Katethong of Thailand. Gunji defeated India’s Tasnim Mir 21-11, 21-11 in the quarter-finals, ending her campaign. Earlier, Tasnim had caused an upset by defeating sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour of Scotland in the pre-quarter-finals. In mixed doubles, India’s Satwik Reddy Kanapuram and Resika Uthayasooryan defeated compatriots Viraj Kuvale and Rituparna Panda 21-8, 21-14 to enter the semi-finals. They will face Malaysia’s pair of V. Y. Hern and Vani Gobi in the last four.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi Shares Devotional Chant to Lord Murugan Amid Thiruparankundram Deepam Row
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a devotional message invoking Lord Murugan, hours after the Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit at the Deepathoon pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district on Saturday. In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared the traditional Tamil devotional chant, “Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara!”, written in English, Tamil and Hindi scripts. The post did not directly refer to the Supreme Court’s order or the ongoing dispute over the lamp-lighting ceremony. The Supreme Court on Friday directed that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the Deepathoon on November 28, following the failure to implement its earlier November 20 order. The court also initiated contempt proceedings against senior Tamil Nadu officials, including the Chief Secretary and Director General of Police, and issued notices to 13 others over alleged non-compliance. The bench suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple and appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to oversee its administration and ensure implementation of the directions. It also directed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to provide security to the temple and the nearby dargah. The court stipulated that the lamp-lighting arrangement should maintain a distance of at least 50 metres from the dargah. BJP holds lamp-lighting programmes across Tamil Nadu Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu BJP Vice-President K.P. Ramalingam criticised the state government over the controversy and welcomed the Supreme Court’s intervention. Participating in the party’s ‘Aram Kaakum Alay Deepam’ programme in Rasipuram in Namakkal district, Ramalingam joined party workers in a procession carrying lamps from near the Anjaneyar Temple to the Arulmigu Nithya Sumangali Mariamman Temple, where prayers were offered and a lamp was lit. Speaking to reporters, he said the BJP had organised similar programmes across Tamil Nadu ahead of the scheduled November 28 ceremony to press for implementation of the Supreme Court’s directions. He claimed that lamps were lit at 2,116 temples under the campaign. Ramalingam accused the state government of failing to respect the court’s earlier order and criticised the Madurai District Collector’s position in the matter. He also made allegations against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s government over its handling of the controversy and the state’s law and order situation. The BJP leader said the party’s campaign would continue, while appealing to the Chief Minister to ensure compliance with the court’s directions. -IANS

national_raw_news.title: India, EU Reaffirm Commitment to Ukraine Peace, Indo-Pacific Stability and Counterterrorism
national_raw_news.content: India and the European Union (EU) have called for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine, strongly condemned terrorism and cross-border terrorism, and reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open and peaceful Indo-Pacific. These issues featured prominently during the 12th India-EU Foreign Policy and Security Consultations (FPSC) held in New Delhi on Friday. The consultations were co-chaired by Secretary (West) in the Ministry of External Affairs, Sibi George, and Olof Skoog, Deputy Secretary General for Political Affairs of the European External Action Service. In a joint statement, both sides underlined the need for a comprehensive and lasting resolution to the Ukraine conflict in accordance with international law and the principles of the United Nations Charter. They also exchanged views on restoring freedom of navigation in the Black Sea, citing its importance for global food security and international trade. The two sides unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all their forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism. Focus on Indo-Pacific and global security India and the EU stressed the importance of closer coordination to address common security challenges and promote regional stability. They reiterated their support for a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific based on international law, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and peaceful resolution of disputes. Amid challenges to multilateralism and international law, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the UN Charter and emphasised the need for an effective multilateral system with the United Nations at its core. Defence partnership and strategic cooperation The consultations reviewed the momentum in India-EU relations and explored ways to deepen the partnership under the ‘Towards 2030: A Joint India-European Union Comprehensive Strategic Agenda’, endorsed at the 16th India-EU Summit in January 2026. Discussions on security and defence cooperation covered maritime security, defence industry and technology, cyber and hybrid threats, space and counterterrorism. Both sides welcomed the inaugural India-EU Security and Defence Dialogue held in New Delhi in March 2026 and noted the progress towards concluding the India-EU Security of Information Agreement. They agreed to hold the second edition of the dialogue next year. Describing each other as trusted, predictable and like-minded partners, India and the EU reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening ties through regular high-level exchanges and established institutional mechanisms. The consultations also reviewed preparations for upcoming meetings at the Leaders’ level. Both sides agreed to hold the next round of Foreign Policy and Security Consultations in Brussels next year, at a mutually convenient date. -ANI
